# geometric_configuration_signature — Intention

## Rationale

The sensor calibration procedure aligns the sensor against the
*primary field generated by the 4 spheres* — so any asymmetry in how the
spheres are physically mounted (caliper-measured diameters and pairwise
distances, `excitation.sources_geometry` in `aefi_device_config.json`) leaks
into the calibrated angles. A calibration entry recorded against one
mounting is not valid for another: if the spheres are ever re-measured after
reassembly, old entries must not be silently reused as if the geometry
hadn't changed (see `EVENT - 2026-09-11_calibration-aefi-comme-agregat-ddd`,
which already flagged this exact risk of mixing geometry and calibration
from different dates).

Without this VO, `SensorCalibrationEntry` would only be taggable by
`HardwareSignature` (board/sensor versions) — which says nothing about which
physical sphere mounting was in place, so a stale calibration could be
matched against the wrong geometry silently.

## Responsibility

- Snapshot the raw caliper values (`sphere_diameters_m`, S1..S4;
  `pairwise_distances_ext_m`, the 6 D_ij) at the moment a calibration entry
  is recorded — not the derived center-to-center distances, not the GUM
  uncertainty metadata (out of scope for calibration matching).
- Compare by value (frozen dataclass of tuples): two entries recorded
  against the same physical mounting have an identical signature
  automatically, no explicit version/id field needed.

## Design

- `@dataclass(frozen=True)`.
- `sphere_diameters_m: Tuple[float, float, float, float]` — order S1, S2, S3, S4.
- `pairwise_distances_ext_m: Tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float]`
  — order D_S1_S2, D_S3_S4, D_S1_S3, D_S1_S4, D_S2_S3, D_S2_S4 (same order as
  `aefi_device_config.json`).
- `__post_init__` only checks tuple arity (4 and 6) — no physical-plausibility
  validation, matching `HardwareSignatureReader`'s tolerant style upstream in
  `GeometricConfigurationReader`.
